dead_ends.approach: Anchor gold-record integrity on a committed manifest alone.
dead_ends.why_failed: A legacy repo has no manifest; git mv/rm + commit removed evidence from git's CURRENT tree with nothing left to compare.

dead_ends.approach: Decide whether to invoke the gold gate by reading git ls-files (the index).
dead_ends.why_failed: A staged-but-uncommitted git rm empties the index, so the suite skipped the gate while it still failed run directly. git log (history) is immune to staging state.

dead_ends.approach: Compare worktree bytes to git's committed blob without EOL normalization.
dead_ends.why_failed: core.autocrlf=true (Git for Windows default) converts the worktree copy; an honest untouched clone was accused of forging its own security sign-off.

dead_ends.approach: Recommend a pre-commit hook running doctrine_gold gate.
dead_ends.why_failed: The gate compares against HEAD, and a record has no HEAD copy until AFTER its own promoting commit exists, so a correct hook refuses the commit that files the first record.

dead_ends.approach: Treat 'CI running this gate on the pushed commit' as a second anchor beyond local checks.
dead_ends.why_failed: CI checks out the identical HEAD a single-commit forgery was committed to and reaches the identical wrong answer. It adds nothing for that class.

dead_ends.approach: Chase every verifier finding into another round, uncapped.
dead_ends.why_failed: Rounds 1-3 were the SAME error class (shell bypass); the thrash detector should have fired after round 2, not round 3.

dead_ends.approach: naive commit-map parse + bare str.replace for sha remapping
dead_ends.why_failed: the map's 'old new' header became a substring rule rewriting English words across eight docs; strict 40-hex validation + word-boundary regex replaced it

dead_ends.approach: codemonk console script directly after pip install on this host
dead_ends.why_failed: Scripts dir not on PATH in this shell; python -m codemonk is the reliable invocation and what the integration doc teaches

learned.claim: A record forged and committed in ONE commit is undetectable by any HEAD-relative check - no prior state exists to diff against.
Circular verification: hashing a claim against data the same artifact supplies verifies nothing. Round 4's gate did this against its own record.
Deletion/relocation is caught by checking git HISTORY (git log) on the path, not only the current HEAD tree or a committed manifest.
A bounded final verification round (one verifier, explicit MUST-FIX/DOCUMENT split) is a reusable pattern for ending a verification arc deliberately.
